themes_detail.label: Street Infrastructure Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints surged to 36 THIS WEEK—a 465% spike above the 6.4 weekly average—while dangling street signs jumped 1767% (7 complaints this week vs. 0.4 weekly average), signaling rapid deterioration of public right-of-way infrastructure in Crown Heights.
evidence: Street condition complaints: 36 this week vs. 6.4 weekly average (465% increase, z-score 8.22)
Dangling street signs: 7 complaints this week vs. 0.4 weekly average (1767% increase, z-score 13.68)
455 DOB permits filed in last 90 days (293 alterations), suggesting ongoing construction activity may be degrading streets
reporting_angles: Which DOT districts/blocks in Crown Heights have the worst street conditions and are repair crews responding?
Are dangling signs a safety hazard—has anyone been injured, and what's the timeline for replacement?

themes_detail.label: Asbestos Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: Asbestos complaints tripled THIS WEEK to 3 complaints versus a 0.5 weekly average—a 500% spike—raising concerns about aging building stock and whether property owners are conducting required environmental assessments before renovation.
evidence: Asbestos complaints: 3 this week vs. 0.5 weekly average (500% increase, z-score 5.0)
82 new building permits and 293 alterations filed in last 90 days, creating renovation activity that may trigger asbestos exposure
CB budget repeatedly requests 'assign additional building inspectors' (unsolved recurring issue), suggesting DOB capacity gap
reporting_angles: Are DOB inspectors keeping pace with renovation activity? How many properties in Crown Heights have pending asbestos certifications?
Interview residents in buildings where asbestos was flagged—what was the remediation timeline and cost?

themes_detail.label: Sanitation and Street Cleanliness Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Over the past 2 weeks, dirty condition complaints spiked 291% (86 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 22.0 weekly average) and street sweeping complaints jumped 700% (6 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.8 weekly average), indicating a breakdown in sanitation services across the district.
evidence: Dirty condition complaints: 86 two weeks ago vs. 22.0 weekly average (291% increase, z-score 5.44)
Street sweeping complaints: 6 two weeks ago vs. 0.8 weekly average (700% increase, z-score 6.33)
Unsanitary condition remains top 5 complaint category at 650 complaints over 90 days, indicating persistent baseline problem
reporting_angles: Has the Sanitation Department reduced street sweeping schedules in Crown Heights? Which blocks are most affected?
Are illegal dumpsites or commercial waste issues driving the dirty condition spike?

themes_detail.label: Noise Complaint Wave
themes_detail.summary: Over the past 2 weeks, noise complaints surged across multiple categories: commercial noise up 124% (39 vs. 17.4 weekly average), vehicle noise up 282% (32 vs. 8.4 weekly average), and general noise up 177% (54 vs. 19.5 weekly average), suggesting new sources of disruption.
evidence: Commercial noise: 39 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 17.4 weekly average (124% increase, z-score 5.59)
Vehicle noise: 32 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 8.4 weekly average (282% increase, z-score 5.35)
General noise: 54 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 19.5 weekly average (177% increase, z-score 4.77)
455 active DOB permits (construction-related activity) may be driving increased vehicle and commercial noise
reporting_angles: Is new construction or commercial activity in specific blocks (e.g., Atlantic Ave FRESH project) driving noise complaints?
How is NYPD responding to noise enforcement given the recent Gothamist article questioning police liability?

themes_detail.label: Building Inspection Capacity Gap
themes_detail.summary: The community board has repeatedly requested additional building inspectors for years (unsolved recurring budget request), and this week's 1767% spike in street sign complaints plus 500% asbestos spike suggest DOB cannot keep pace with 455 active permits and aging infrastructure in Crown Heights.
evidence: CB budget request '[01] Assign additional building inspectors (including expanding training programs)' is recurring/unsolved
455 DOB permits filed in last 90 days (293 alterations, 82 new buildings)
Asbestos complaints: 3 this week vs. 0.5 average (500% spike); dangling street signs: 7 this week vs. 0.4 average (1767% spike)
reporting_angles: What is DOB's current inspector-to-permit ratio in CD 308? How long does a typical alteration permit inspection take?
Has the city responded to the community board's multi-year request for additional inspectors, and if not, why?
